title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 137 (Copy of financial statement to be filed with Registrar)

content.overview: A copy of the financial statements, including consolidated financial statement if any, along with all the documents which are required to be attached to such financial statements under this Act, duly adopted at the annual general meeting of the company, shall be filed with the Registrar within thirty days of the date of annual general meeting in such manner, with such fees or additional fees as may be prescribed. A One Person Company files within one hundred and eighty days from the close of the financial year.
content.glance: Adopted financial statements (including consolidated) are filed with the Registrar within thirty days of the AGM; OPC has one hundred and eighty days from year-end.
content.study:
## Section 137 — Filing of financial statements

**General rule.** File a copy of the financial statements (including consolidated), with all required attached documents, duly adopted at the AGM, with the Registrar within thirty days of the AGM.

**Not adopted / meeting not held.** Unadopted statements are filed within thirty days of the meeting date or the last date before which the meeting should have been held, stating the reasons; adopted statements follow.

**OPC.** A One Person Company files within one hundred and eighty days from the closure of the financial year.

Circulation to members is section 136; content and standards are section 129.

This note is a focused study aid; the topic remains under source and current-law review.

sections.heading: Thirty-day filing
sections.body: Adopted financial statements filed with the Registrar within thirty days of the AGM.

sections.heading: OPC and unadopted
sections.body: OPC: 180 days from year-end. Unadopted: file with reasons within thirty days of the relevant date.

examples.title: Post-AGM filing
examples.body: Company adopts financial statements at AGM and files with the Registrar within thirty days. Educational illustration.

hypotheticals.question: Is the thirty-day period measured from the financial year-end?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. For a company other than an OPC, the period is thirty days from the date of the annual general meeting. OPC has 180 days from year-end.

misconceptions.correction: Section 136 is pre-meeting circulation to members; section 137 is post-AGM filing with the Registrar.

questionsAndAnswers.question: When must financial statements be filed under section 137?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Within thirty days of the AGM for a company other than an OPC; within 180 days from the close of the financial year for an OPC.
